page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by 192 dedicated physical cores running on 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 AWS Graviton processors clocked at 2.7 GHz, with no simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system features a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio, providing 384.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per core). It also incorporates 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. No graphics processing units are included in this hardware configuration.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional throughput in highly parallel environments, contrasting with moderate single-threaded performance. In multi-core testing, the instance reaches top-tier results in stress-ng (311,373.11) and Geekbench multi-core (20,654.0), alongside top-tier metrics for software compilation with Clang (86,720.0), ray tracing (134,235.0), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (1,367.53 GB/sec). Conversely, Geekbench single-core (1,656.0) and stress-ng single-core (1,643.88) align with mid-range averages. Memory throughput reaches top-tier marks with uncached read speeds of 907.71 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 402.56 GB/sec.

Data-intensive and web serving benchmarks demonstrate massive concurrent capacity, posting 362.69 million Redis SET operations per second and 169.75 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. PassMark database operations also place in the top tier at 46,609.13. For language model workloads without discrete accelerators, prompt processing reaches strong tiers on medium 7B models at 184.84 tokens/sec, but drops to weak tiers on small 135M models (285.67 tokens/sec) and average tiers on 70B models (22.5 tokens/sec).

Qualitatively, the c8gd.48xlarge offers high computational and storage density per resource unit by combining 192 physical Graviton cores with fast local NVMe storage and high memory bandwidth. The architecture is best suited for horizontally parallel compute pipelines, distributed databases, large-scale Clang code builds, high-throughput caching layers, and high-concurrency static web delivery where single-thread clock speed is secondary to aggregate multithreaded capacity.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gd.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by 192 physical ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 Graviton cores at 2.7 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 384.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), 11,400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage, and 50 Gbps baseline networking, it targets massive multithreaded and I/O-intensive workloads without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results emphasize its scaling advantages: stress-ng multi-core (311,373.11), Geekbench multi-core (20,654.0), and Clang compilation (86,720.0) reach the top 10%, while single-core scores remain in the average tier. It also posts exceptional memory bandwidth (907.71 GB/sec uncached read) and tops Redis operations (362.69 million ops/sec). The c8gd.48xlarge provides high resource density, making it well fitted for software compilation, high-concurrency web serving, in-memory databases, and distributed parallel batch processing.
